title: SkeletonKey ToolManifest
description: What a tool must declare to join the registry. Written by hand for built-ins, by an author for a skill/drop-in, and read by the advertisement step that decides what a host is offered on this host, for this task. Field names here are the on-disk names in tool.toml / SKILL.md tool blocks and the keys of `registry.describe`.

id.description: group.name, lowercase, dot-separated. The registry is flat, so the group prefix is what keeps 100 tools navigable.

version.description: Bumped when the schema or semantics change; part of the idempotency key.

description.description: Written for a model under time pressure: what it does, when NOT to use it, and the one gotcha. This is the highest-leverage text in the system.

group.description: Defaults to the id prefix. A skill-authored tool gets 'skill.<name>'.

capability.description: What has to be true for this tool to run here (fs.patch.gnu, shell.powershell, search.ripgrep...). Gating and routing both work off this, not off the name.

provides.description: Capabilities this tool contributes (a provider can satisfy one for others).

provider.description: Backing implementation, when the tool is one of several for a capability (rg vs the built-in walker).

priority.description: Higher wins when two tools advertise the same capability.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for the arguments. Enforced by the engine before the handler runs, and forwarded verbatim to MCP hosts.

output_schema.description: Optional. Documented data keys of the envelope's `data` field.

requirements.description: All must hold (AND) for the tool to be advertised here.

require_any.description: At least one must hold (OR). Used by shell.run: any usable dialect is enough.

platforms.description: Empty = every platform the host runs on.

tags.description: Routing vocabulary: natural-language synonyms the agent is likely to type ('rm', 'unlink', 'clean').

risk.description: Drives auto-approval, read_only withholding, MCP annotations, and the ledger's audit level.

idempotent.description: Same args, no side effects. Enables the short-TTL result cache - never set it for something that polls state.

open_world.description: Touches things outside the sandbox (network, other processes). Sets MCP's openWorldHint.

destructive.description: Loses data the user did not create in this run. Never bypassable by approval alone unless confirm_destructive is off.

reversible.description: A journal entry makes undo possible; the host is told, so it can offer 'undo' as a first-class action.

typical_latency_ms.description: Used to order parallel batches and to decide what gets backgrounded.

typical_output_bytes.description: Budget planning input: 30 of these is a context-window decision, not a runtime one.

stateful.description: 'none' is what makes result caching legal. shell.sessions is a pure read and still must not be cached.

advertised.description: false = callable but hidden (skill-declared stubs awaiting Phase 2 synthesis, internal tools).

hidden_reason.description: Set by the registry when advertisement withheld the tool, so `registry.list {include_gated: true}` can explain why.

examples.description: Returned as `minimal_example` on a BAD_ARGS failure: the fastest possible recovery for an agent.

anti_patterns.description: 'do not use this when X' - cheaper than a failed call.

see_also.description: Tool ids that usually follow or replace this one; surfaced as next_actions.

source_path.description: Where a non-built-in manifest came from. Doubles as the trust signal in the security model.

meta.description: Free-form. MCP hosts receive it under _meta.sk.

name.description: What to look for: an executable, an env var, a profile capability id, an OS.

min_version.description: Dotted, compared numerically; a probe that cannot answer fails the requirement.

optional.description: Recorded in the receipt, but does not withhold the tool.
